questions.p: Marginal cost na the change for total cost divide by the change for quantity. So (₦84,500 - ₦82,000) / 1 = ₦2,500.

questions.q: A cassava processing firm in Enugu has a total fixed cost of ₦45,000, which does not change with the level of output. At what level of output will the firm's average fixed cost (AFC) equal exactly ₦150 per unit?
questions.e: Average fixed cost is total fixed cost divided by quantity, so AFC = TFC/Q. Setting 150 = 45,000/Q and solving gives Q = 45,000/150 = 300 units.
questions.p: Average fixed cost na total fixed cost divide by quantity, so AFC = TFC/Q. If we put 150 = 45,000/Q, we go solve am make Q = 45,000/150 = 300 units.

questions.q: Which of the following is a distinguishing structural feature of a monopoly market, as opposed to perfect competition?
o: Firms are price takers with no control over price
Entry and exit of firms are completely free
There are many firms producing identical products
There is only one firm in the industry producing a product with no close substitute
questions.e: A monopoly exists when a single firm controls the entire supply of a product that has no close substitute, and entry is usually blocked. This is different from perfect competition, where many firms sell identical goods and entry is free.
questions.p: Monopoly na when one company dey control the whole market and nobody fit easily enter the business, plus the product no get close substitute. For perfect competition, na plenty companies dey sell the same type of goods and anybody fit enter.

questions.q: A perfectly competitive firm in Kano sells groundnut oil at the prevailing market price of ₦100 per unit. Its total cost function is TC = 20Q + 2Q^2, where Q is the quantity produced per day. What output level maximizes the firm's profit?
questions.e: Under perfect competition, profit is maximized where Marginal Cost (MC) equals Price (since P = MR). MC = d(TC)/dQ = 20 + 4Q. Setting 20 + 4Q = 100 gives 4Q = 80, so Q = 20 units.
questions.p: For perfect competition, profit dey maximum when Marginal Cost (MC) equal Price. MC = 20 + 4Q, so if you set am equal to 100, 4Q go be 80, and Q go be 20 units.

questions.q: In Nigeria's cement industry, suppose four leading firms control the following percentages of total market sales: Firm A, 40%; Firm B, 25%; Firm C, 20%; Firm D, 10%, while many small firms share the remaining 5%. What is the four-firm concentration ratio (CR4) of this market, and what type of market structure does this ratio suggest?
questions.e: The four-firm concentration ratio is found by adding the market shares of the four largest firms: 40% + 25% + 20% + 10% = 95%. A CR4 this high (close to total market control by a few firms) is typical of an oligopoly, not perfect competition or pure monopoly.
questions.p: To find CR4, you just add the market share of the four biggest companies: 40% + 25% + 20% + 10% = 95%. Since few companies dey control almost everything, na oligopoly be dis, no be perfect competition or pure monopoly.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best defines Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
o: The total income received by a country's citizens after deducting taxes and adding subsidies
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country after deducting depreciation of capital
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a country in a given year, regardless of the nationality of the producers
The total market value of all final goods and services produced by the citizens of a country, whether at home or abroad, in a given year
questions.e: GDP measures the total value of final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year, no matter who produced them (citizens or foreigners). The other options describe GNP, NNP, and disposable income instead of GDP.
questions.p: GDP na di total value of all final goods and services wey dem produce inside one country border for one year, no matter who produce am (citizen or foreigner). The other options dey describe GNP, NNP or disposable income instead.

questions.q: In a given year, Nigeria's GDP was ₦500 billion. The net factor income from abroad was negative ₦20 billion, meaning foreigners earned more income from activities in Nigeria than Nigerians earned abroad. If capital depreciation for the year was ₦40 billion, what was the Net National Product (NNP) for that year?
questions.e: First find GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 500 + (-20) = ₦480 billion. Then NNP = GNP - depreciation = 480 - 40 = ₦440 billion.
questions.p: First find GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad = 500 + (-20) = 480 billion naira. Then minus depreciation make e be NNP = 480 - 40 = 440 billion naira.

questions.q: An economics teacher in Kaduna told her students that when national income is correctly computed using the output, income, and expenditure methods, all three approaches should give the same total value for a given year. Which of the following best explains why this equality holds?
o: Because indirect taxes are automatically added to all three methods before final computation
Because what is spent by one group of economic agents becomes income to another group, which in turn equals the value of output produced
Because national income statisticians always round off figures to the nearest billion naira
Because government deliberately adjusts the three figures to match international standards
questions.e: National income flows in a circle: firms produce output, which is sold for money (expenditure), and that money becomes income for workers and resource owners (income). Because of this circular flow, the output, income, and expenditure methods should, in theory, all add up to the same total.
questions.p: National income dey flow like circle: company produce output, dem sell am for money (expenditure), and dat money come become income for worker and resource owner (income). Because of dis circle flow, output, income and expenditure method suppose give the same total value.

questions.q: Chief Nwosu sold his yams and kept part of the proceeds in a savings account so that he could use the money to pay his daughter's school fees two years later. This use of money is best described as money performing the function of a:
questions.e: Money acts as a store of value when it is kept aside to be used for spending in the future without losing (much) of its usefulness. Chief Nwosu is saving the money to use later, so this is the store of value function, not buying something now (medium of exchange) or pricing goods (unit of account).
questions.p: Money dey work as store of value when person keep am well-well to use am later, no be to buy something now-now. Since Chief Nwosu kon save the money make e use am two years later, na store of value be dis, no be unit of account or medium of exchange.

questions.q: In an economy, the total money supply is ₦200,000,000 and the velocity of circulation of money is 5. If the total output of goods and services produced in the economy is 2,500,000 units, use the Quantity Theory of Money (MV = PQ) to find the average price level per unit.
questions.e: Using MV = PQ, P = MV/Q = (200,000,000 x 5) / 2,500,000 = 1,000,000,000 / 2,500,000 = ₦400. This is the only value that satisfies the equation with the given figures.
questions.p: Dem use MV=PQ formula: P = MV/Q = (200,000,000 x 5) / 2,500,000 = ₦400. Na di correct answer wey match di figures wey dem give.

questions.q: A commercial bank in Lagos offers a nominal interest rate of 15 percent per annum on fixed deposits, while the prevailing inflation rate in the economy is 9 percent per annum. Using the simple Fisher relationship (Nominal rate = Real rate + Inflation rate), what is the approximate real interest rate earned by a depositor?
questions.e: From the Fisher equation, Real rate = Nominal rate - Inflation rate = 15% - 9% = 6%. This shows the true increase in the depositor's purchasing power after accounting for inflation, which is lower than the nominal rate quoted by the bank.
questions.p: From Fisher equation, Real rate = Nominal rate minus Inflation rate = 15% - 9% = 6%. Na dis one show di real power wey depositor get after dem remove inflation, e dey smaller pass di nominal rate wey bank talk.

questions.q: Which of the following is a money market instrument commonly used by the Nigerian government to raise short-term funds?
questions.e: Treasury bills are short-term debt securities issued by government and traded in the money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares are long-term securities traded in the capital market.
questions.p: Treasury bills na short-term paper wey government dey issue for money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares na long-term things wey dem dey trade for capital market.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes how commercial banks create credit in an economy?
o: Banks lend out a fraction of their deposits while keeping the rest as reserve, thereby expanding the total money supply
Banks print new currency notes to meet customer withdrawal demand
Banks transfer all customer deposits to the Central Bank for safekeeping
Banks exchange foreign currency for local currency on behalf of customers
questions.e: Commercial banks keep only a small fraction of deposits as reserve and lend out the rest. As this lent money is redeposited and relent, the total money supply in the economy expands, a process called credit creation.
questions.p: Commercial banks go keep small part of the money as reserve, then dem go loan out the rest. As dis money dey enter and comot again, e dey increase the total money wey dey circulate - na so credit creation dey work.

questions.q: Public debt can be classified based on the source of borrowing. Which of the following best describes an external public debt?
o: Money borrowed from citizens through the sale of treasury bills
Money owed by government to local contractors for completed projects
Money borrowed from foreign governments and international financial institutions such as the World Bank
Money borrowed by government from the Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.e: External debt is money a government owes to lenders outside the country, such as foreign governments or bodies like the World Bank. Internal debt, on the other hand, is owed to lenders within the country, such as citizens or the central bank.
questions.p: External debt na money wey government borrow from outside country, like foreign government or World Bank. Internal debt na money wey government borrow from inside the country, like citizens or CBN.

questions.q: Mallam Sule's taxable annual income is ₦3,200,000. Under a progressive tax system, the first ₦800,000 of taxable income is taxed at 7%, the next ₦1,000,000 is taxed at 11%, and any amount above ₦1,800,000 is taxed at 15%. Calculate Mallam Sule's total tax payable for the year.
questions.p: Step by step: first 800k dem tax 7% e give 56,000. Next 1,000,000 dem tax 11% e give 110,000. Wetin remain na 1,400,000 (3,200,000 minus 1,800,000), dem tax am 15% e give 210,000. If you add everything you go get 376,000.

questions.q: In a particular fiscal year, the Federal Government of Nigeria budgeted total expenditure of ₦61 billion while total revenue collected was ₦45 billion. To finance the shortfall, the government obtained a loan of ₦10 billion from a development bank, and the remaining balance was financed by drawing down its reserves. How much was drawn from the reserves?
questions.e: Budget deficit = expenditure - revenue = 61 - 45 = 16 billion. The loan already covers 10 billion of this deficit, so the amount drawn from reserves = 16 - 10 = 6 billion.
questions.p: Budget deficit na wetin dem spend minus wetin dem collect: 61-45=16 billion. Dem don already get loan of 10 billion, so wetin remain wey go come from reserves na 16-10=6 billion.

questions.q: According to Rostow's stages of economic growth theory, which stage describes a society that still depends mainly on traditional methods of farming and production, with low savings and little technological change, and has not yet begun the process of self-sustained growth?
questions.e: Rostow described the traditional society stage as one where output is limited by old farming methods, low savings, and little science or technology. This is the first and most basic stage before any serious growth begins.
questions.p: Rostow talk say for traditional society stage, people dey use old farming way, savings dey small, and dem never start real growth. Na the first and most basic stage before any serious change.

questions.q: Last year, a certain West African country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was ₦120 trillion. This year, it rose to ₦126 trillion. What is the country's economic growth rate for the year?
questions.e: Growth rate = (New GDP - Old GDP) / Old GDP x 100. That is (126 - 120)/120 x 100 = 6/120 x 100 = 5%. So the economy grew by 5% that year.
questions.p: Growth rate = (New GDP - Old GDP) divide by Old GDP, times 100. So na (126-120)/120 x 100 = 5%. The economy grow by 5% for that year.

questions.q: In Nigeria, 'mixed farming' is best described as a system in which a farmer
o: practises only animal husbandry on a ranch
cultivates crops and rears livestock together on the same farm
grows only tree crops for export
plants a single crop across several hectares of land
questions.e: Mixed farming means combining crop production with livestock rearing on the same farm. This helps the farmer use resources like manure and crop residue efficiently. It is common among small-scale farmers in Nigeria.
questions.p: Mixed farming na when farmer dey plant crops and still dey rear animals for the same farm. E help farmer use manure and leftover crops well well. Na common practice for Nigeria small farmers.

questions.q: In a certain year, Nigeria's total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was valued at ₦200 billion, while the agricultural sector contributed ₦50 billion to this total. What percentage of the GDP did agriculture contribute that year?
questions.e: Percentage contribution = (Agricultural output / Total GDP) x 100 = (50/200) x 100 = 25%. This shows how economists measure a sector's share of national output.
questions.p: Percentage wey agriculture contribute = (50/200) x 100 = 25%. Na so dem dey calculate how much one sector dey contribute to total GDP.

questions.q: Large-scale rural-urban migration of young, able-bodied men in search of white-collar jobs has been a persistent feature of the Nigerian economy. What is the most likely direct economic consequence of this trend on commercial crop farming in rural areas?
o: A rise in the cost of farm labour due to reduced supply of workers
A fall in the cost of farm labour due to oversupply of workers
An automatic increase in farm mechanization funded by migrants
A reduction in the demand for food in urban markets
questions.e: When young workers leave rural areas, the supply of farm labour falls while demand for labour on farms stays roughly the same. By basic supply and demand reasoning, a fall in supply with steady demand pushes up the price (wage) of farm labour, raising production costs for farmers.
questions.p: When young people dey comot from village go city, the number of people wey dey available to work for farm dey reduce. Demand for farm labour no change reach like that, so wetin dey happen be say cost of hiring farm workers go rise, and e go cost farmer more money.

questions.q: Mama Ngozi's bakery buys flour, sugar and other light ingredients, but the baked bread that comes out is bulkier and heavier to transport in large quantities to many customers across town. Based on the theory of industrial location, where would such a bakery most likely be sited to reduce cost?
o: Close to the river that supplies water for baking
Close to the flour mill that supplies raw flour
Close to the market where the bread will be sold
questions.e: Industries whose finished products are bulkier or heavier than their raw materials are called weight-gaining industries. They are usually sited near the market to reduce the cost of transporting the heavier finished goods. Bread baking is a good example of this.
questions.p: Industry wey dem dey call weight-gaining dey make product wey heavy pass di raw materials. Dem go rather build near market so dem no go waste money to carry heavy bread go far. Na why bakery dey near market pass raw material source.

questions.q: When a limited liability company is being registered in Nigeria, the document that spells out the internal rules of the company, including how directors are appointed, how meetings are conducted and the rights of shareholders, is known as the:
questions.e: The Memorandum of Association defines the company's relationship with the outside world, such as its name, objectives and capital. The Articles of Association, on the other hand, contain the internal rules guiding how the company is run, including directors' duties and shareholders' rights. This makes option B the correct answer.
questions.p: Memorandum of Association dey show how company relate with outside world, like im name and wetin e wan do. Articles of Association na di one wey get di inside rules like how directors go work and how shareholders go get their rights. So na Articles of Association be di answer.

questions.q: A soft-drink company uses large quantities of water (which is heavy and bulky) to produce its finished bottled drinks, which are even heavier and bulkier than the water and sugar used to make them. Applying the principle of weight-gaining and weight-losing industries to decide factory location, where should this company most likely site its bottling plant?
o: Near the market where the drinks will be sold
Near the source of sugar used in production
Near the seaport where sugar is imported
Exactly halfway between the sugar source and the market
questions.e: Because the finished bottled drinks are heavier and bulkier than the raw materials, this is a weight-gaining industry. Weight-gaining industries locate near the market to avoid the high cost of transporting the heavier finished product over long distances. Locating near raw materials or midway would increase transport cost for the bulkier final goods.
questions.p: Since di finished drinks dey heavier pass di raw materials wey dem use make am, na weight-gaining industry be dis. Weight-gaining industries dey site near market so dem no go spend plenty money to carry di heavy finished product go far. If dem build am near sugar source or for middle, e go cost more to transport di heavier product.

questions.q: In which decade did crude oil overtake agricultural products (like cocoa and groundnut) as Nigeria's leading foreign exchange earner?
questions.e: After the Nigerian Civil War, the oil boom of the 1970s pushed crude oil export earnings far above those from agriculture. Before this, agriculture (cocoa, groundnut, palm produce) was Nigeria's main foreign exchange source.
questions.p: After di civil war, na for 1970s crude oil begin bring plenty money pass agriculture. Before that time na agriculture (cocoa, groundnut) dey bring the main foreign exchange.

questions.q: When a country's heavy reliance on crude oil exports causes its currency to appreciate, making other export goods like cocoa or textiles too expensive for foreign buyers, this economic phenomenon is best described as
questions.e: Dutch Disease occurs when a booming resource sector (like oil) causes currency appreciation, which then hurts other export sectors by making them less price-competitive abroad. This weakens diversification of the economy away from oil.
questions.p: Dutch Disease na wetin dey happen when oil money make naira strong, so e make other exports like cocoa cost too much for foreign buyers. Dis one dey make am hard for economy to depend on something apart from oil.

questions.q: In population studies, what name is given to the official, periodic, and systematic process of counting every person in a country, usually recording details such as age, sex, and occupation, at a specific point in time?
questions.e: A census is the complete count of all persons in a country at a particular time, including details like age, sex and occupation. A sample survey only covers part of the population, while vital registration tracks births/deaths continuously, not a one-time count.
questions.p: Census na di full and official count of everybody for one kontri, dem go record di age, sex and wetin dem dey do. Sample survey no cover everybody, and vital registration na continuous recording, e no be one-time full count.

questions.q: A town in Delta State has a total population of 80,000. Out of this, 20,000 are children aged 0-14 years and 10,000 are elderly persons aged 65 years and above. The remaining people make up the working-age population. What is the dependency ratio of the town, expressed as a percentage?
questions.e: Working-age population = 80,000 - 20,000 - 10,000 = 50,000. Dependency ratio = (children + elderly) / working-age population x 100 = (20,000 + 10,000) / 50,000 x 100 = 60%. This shows that for every 100 working people, there are 60 dependants to support.
questions.p: Working-age people = 80,000 minus 20,000 minus 10,000 = 50,000. Dependency ratio = (children + old people) divide working-age, multiply by 100 = 30,000/50,000 x 100 = 60%. So na 60 dependants for every 100 working people.

questions.q: A developing country's population is growing at a constant annual rate of 2.5%. Using the simple 'Rule of 70' (Doubling time = 70 / annual growth rate), approximately how many years will it take for the country's population to double in size?
questions.e: Using the Rule of 70: Doubling time = 70 / 2.5 = 28 years. This rule gives a quick estimate of how long a growing quantity, like population, takes to double at a given constant percentage growth rate. A higher growth rate always means a shorter doubling time.
questions.p: Dem dey use Rule of 70: Doubling time = 70 divide by 2.5 = 28 years. Dis rule na fast way to sabi how long population go take double if di growth rate no change. If growth rate high pass, e go take shorter time to double.

questions.q: In the study of international trade, which statement correctly describes an IMPROVEMENT in a country's terms of trade?
o: The volume of exports falls while the volume of imports rises
The index of import prices rises faster than the index of export prices
The index of export prices rises faster than the index of import prices
Export prices and import prices rise at exactly the same rate
questions.e: Terms of trade compares how fast export prices change relative to import prices. If export prices rise faster than import prices, a country earns more for each unit it sells abroad compared with what it pays for imports, which is an improvement.
questions.p: Terms of trade na how export price dey move compare to import price. If export price dey rise pass import price, kontri go dey gain more for wetin e dey sell compare to wetin e dey buy, so e don improve.

questions.q: A country's export price index is 150 and its import price index is 120, using the same base year of 100. Calculate the country's terms of trade index.
questions.e: Terms of trade index = (Export price index / Import price index) x 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. A value above 100 shows the terms of trade are favourable, since export prices have risen more than import prices.
questions.p: Terms of trade = (Export price index divide Import price index) times 100 = (150/120) x 100 = 125. Since e pass 100, e mean say the terms of trade favour the kontri well well.

questions.q: Using 1 unit of labour-time, Country Dara can produce either 1 bag of cloth (using 5 hours) or 1 pair of shoes (using 10 hours). Country Kowa can produce either 1 bag of cloth (using 8 hours) or 1 pair of shoes (using 20 hours). Based on the principle of comparative advantage, which country should specialise in producing shoes?
o: Country Dara, because its opportunity cost of shoes (2 bags of cloth) is lower than Country Kowa's (2.5 bags of cloth)
Country Kowa, because it uses more hours to make shoes, showing greater effort and skill
Both countries equally, since they both take longer to make shoes than cloth
Neither country, because Country Dara is more efficient at making both goods
questions.e: Opportunity cost of 1 pair of shoes in Dara = 10 hours / 5 hours per cloth = 2 bags of cloth. In Kowa, it is 20/8 = 2.5 bags of cloth. Since Dara gives up less cloth to make shoes, Dara has the comparative advantage in shoes, even though Dara is also better at cloth (absolute advantage does not decide specialisation, comparative advantage does).
questions.p: Opportunity cost of one shoe for Dara na 10/5 = 2 bags of cloth, but for Kowa na 20/8 = 2.5 bags of cloth. Since Dara dey sacrifice less cloth make e produce shoe, Dara get comparative advantage for shoe, even though Dara sabi make both goods pass Kowa overall.

questions.q: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was formally established in 1975 by the Treaty of Lagos. In which city is the ECOWAS Commission (headquarters) currently located?
questions.e: ECOWAS was founded in Lagos in 1975, but its permanent headquarters (the ECOWAS Commission) is sited in Abuja, Nigeria. The other cities host other regional bodies or were just meeting venues, not the headquarters.
questions.p: Dem form ECOWAS for Lagos for 1975, but di main headquarters (ECOWAS Commission) dey Abuja, Nigeria. Di oda cities no be where di headquarters dey.

questions.q: The World Bank Group has several affiliate institutions with different functions. Which of these institutions specifically provides interest-free loans and grants to the world's poorest developing countries to support social and economic development?
questions.e: The IDA is the arm of the World Bank Group that gives interest-free (concessional) loans and grants to the poorest countries. IFC deals with private sector investment, MIGA provides investment insurance, and the IMF is a separate institution dealing with balance of payments issues, not a World Bank affiliate.
questions.p: IDA na di World Bank arm wey dey give free-interest loan and grant to di poorest kontries. IFC dey support private business, MIGA dey insure investment, and IMF na separate body wey dey handle balance of payment wahala.

questions.q: A developing country's currency has depreciated sharply, causing severe balance of payments difficulties. The government approaches the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for emergency financial assistance. Based on typical IMF loan conditionalities designed to restore macroeconomic stability, which policy package would the country most likely be required to adopt?
o: Reduce government spending and allow further currency adjustment to restore competitiveness
Raise import tariffs sharply to protect local industries from foreign competition
Increase fuel and electricity subsidies to protect citizens from hardship
Nationalise all commercial banks to directly control the money supply
questions.e: IMF conditionalities typically require fiscal discipline (cutting government spending/subsidies) and market-driven exchange rate adjustment to correct balance of payments problems. Increasing subsidies, raising tariffs, or nationalising banks would worsen fiscal deficits or distort markets, which goes against IMF's standard stabilisation approach.
questions.p: IMF dey ask kontri to cut government spending and allow di currency adjust well-well so dem fit become competitive again. To increase subsidy, raise tariff, or nationalise banks go only make di budget wahala and market problem worse, na im be why dem no go gree am.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'collective bargaining' in the labour market?
o: Negotiation between trade union representatives and employers over wages and working conditions
Individual workers bargaining alone with their employer for higher pay
Government fixing wages without consulting employers or workers
Workers forming cooperative societies to produce and sell goods
questions.e: Collective bargaining means trade union leaders negotiate as a group with employers on behalf of all workers, covering issues like wages and conditions of service. This gives workers stronger bargaining power than if they negotiated alone. Options B, C and D describe different, unrelated actions.
questions.p: Collective bargaining na when union leaders dey negotiate as one group with employer about wages and work condition. E dey give workers better power pass if everybody dey negotiate alone. The other options no match this definition.

questions.q: A textile factory in Aba employs 150 workers at a daily wage of ₦2,500 each. After successful negotiation by the workers' trade union, the daily wage rate is increased by 20%. What is the new total daily wage bill of the factory?
questions.e: New wage = 2,500 + (20% of 2,500) = 2,500 + 500 = ₦3,000 per worker. Total wage bill = 150 workers x ₦3,000 = ₦450,000. The other options either use the old wage or wrong percentage increase.
questions.p: New wage be 2,500 add 20% of am (500), e give 3,000 per worker. Multiply am by 150 workers e give ₦450,000. Other options na wrong calculation or dem use old wage.

questions.q: In a hypothetical labour market, the demand for labour is given by Ld = 800 - 2W, and the supply of labour is given by Ls = -100 + 3W, where W is the daily wage rate in Naira and L is the number of workers. If government fixes a minimum wage of ₦200 per day, which is above the market equilibrium wage, how many workers will be unemployed (excess supply) at this wage?
questions.e: At W=200: Ld = 800 - 2(200) = 400, and Ls = -100 + 3(200) = 500. Since supply exceeds demand, unemployment = Ls - Ld = 500 - 400 = 100 workers. This shows how a minimum wage set above equilibrium creates a labour surplus.
